search_row.title: Hawk-Dove mixed ESS
search_row.statement: When the cost of injury exceeds the value of the contested resource, the stable outcome is a mixture in which animals escalate with probability equal to the ratio of resource value to injury cost.
search_row.math: payoffs E(H,H) = (V-C)/2, E(H,D) = V, E(D,H) = 0, E(D,D) = V/2; for C > V the unique ESS plays Hawk with probability p^* = V/C

fields.dct:source: John Maynard Smith (1982) Evolution and the Theory of Games
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Experimentally vary resource value and the expected cost of fighting in a contest system, and test that escalation frequency tracks V/C.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: symmetric pairwise contests, fixed V and C, no role asymmetries (asymmetries such as ownership give the Bourgeois ESS instead). Formal status: proved within the game.
